topics.topic: Artifacts that must be absent or discarded after the refused trace write
questions: Does “none” mean only that no trace record exists, or that the failed attempt leaves no output value, node state, resource accounting, trial evidence, or other durable record of any kind?
Does the failed trace write leave only no trace record, or must the function's output value, digest, scheduling changes and any other execution artifacts also be absent or removed atomically?
What happens to the first execution's output and any produced spool file when its trace record is refused?

judgement.why: This is the same question about retention and visibility of artifacts from an unrecorded function execution, and the relevant texts have not changed since P10.

precedent.topic: Visibility, retention, and cleanup of outputs and artifacts from an unrecorded execution
quotes:
A call that fails writes and changes no record; the only
trace it can leave is a published file no record names, which nothing reads:
a spooled file is replaced at its position, value bytes are reused by equal
bytes until the next start removes them (rule 4).

A non-empty list has no
record of its own: the elements' NodeExecutions are its durable facts, and
the list — its StoredValue identity, its files, its class — is derived from
them in element order whenever it is delivered, after a restart too, and
then named by every record that receives it.
precedent.why: State 2 makes concluded records the delivery facts and makes an orphaned file unreadable, replaceable or removable, so an unrecorded output cannot be delivered as a concluded result.

topics.topic: Atomic ordering of trace durability and output publication to dependants
questions: Are the function output, node completion, trace record, and release of data to dependants committed atomically, so that no dependant can consume the first attempt's output before its trace is refused?
May a function output be delivered to dependent nodes before its immutable trace record is successfully stored?
Must the trace record become durable before the function output can be validated, stored, placed in the spool, or exposed to any downstream node?

judgement.why: This is the same question about publishing or delivering function output before its trace record is durable, and the relevant texts have not changed since P3.

precedent.topic: Whether function outputs may be published before the trace record is durable

topics.topic: Caller-visible stop, run or node status, and call outcome after trace refusal
questions: Does “the kernel stops” mean the process terminates, the node attempt aborts, or the run call returns a refusal, and what observable run status and response does the caller receive?
How can the call satisfy K-17's succeed-or-refuse rule when K-09 says the kernel stops, and which passage governs the caller-visible outcome?
What exactly stops when the trace record is refused, and what observable failure is returned to an active caller?
What persisted and surface-visible state does the run have between the refused trace write and successful recovery?
What observable run or node state represents this stop, and how does it relate to the stated rule that no wait ends by itself?

quotes:
A store failure can leave a run's stored status behind its records. Any
request answered `internal_error` therefore stops the kernel once the
answer is sent, so the next start derives every run (rule 5) before any
request touches one.

On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
   `in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
   run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
   from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
   waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
   outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
   kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`:

| `internal_error` | the failing store change wrote nothing; changes the request made before it stay (Conventions); no detail (A16 rule 7) | the caller re-reads before repeating; the owner reads the host log |
judgement.why: The later rules say the active request receives internal_error before the process stops, permit the stored run status to lag, and require startup derivation to repair and advance it before the surface reopens.

topics.topic: Meaning and scope of the recovery having no effect
questions: What exactly “has no effect”: the failed first execution, the act of recovery, or the recovery execution's external side effects, and does the recovery execution still publish its declared output?

What does "has no effect" promise when K-02 permits admitted function code whose outputs may depend on undisclosed time or chance: only no external side effect, or also no observable difference from the lost execution?
What does “which has no effect” refer to, and does “effect” exclude the function's declared output?

quotes:
On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
   `in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
   run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
   from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
   waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
   outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
   kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`: a
   function element without a
   concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect;

Every concluded attempt at an element, every skipped node and every
   `upstream_failed` node writes exactly one NodeExecution M23 — an owner's
   resolution of an unknown outcome writes none (A11).

The trace record of one concluded attempt at one node, or of a node that was not
executed because its guards disabled it or an upstream node failed (K-09). Read by the owner
and agents reading traces, by repair (K-12) and by capture into a trial corpus.
judgement.why: The later rules use no effect to justify rerunning a function, while the recovered execution that obtains the single concluded NodeExecution supplies the recorded output and conclusion.

questions: What concrete recovery action starts the re-execution, who performs or requests it, and when may it occur?
Who or what starts recovery, when does it run, and how does it identify the unrecorded function execution that must be repeated?
Who or what initiates recovery, when does it occur, and is an owner or agent request required?

judgement.why: This is the same question about the recovery trigger, actor, and timing, and the relevant texts have not changed since P7.

quotes:
On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
`in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`:
precedent.why: State 2 makes recovery automatic at process start, performed by the kernel before the surface accepts requests.

topics.topic: Retry and terminal behavior when recovery trace writes are repeatedly refused
questions: What happens if the store refuses the recovery execution's trace record as well: repeated automatic recovery, a pending run, a failed run, or a caller-visible refusal?
What happens if the store refuses the recovered execution's trace record again, including when the refusal is permanent rather than transient?
What happens if the store also refuses the recovery execution's trace record, including whether retries are automatic, bounded, or terminal?

judgement.why: This is the same question about repeated or permanent refusal of the recovered execution's trace write, and the relevant texts have not changed since P8.

precedent.topic: Retry policy and terminal state for repeated or permanent trace refusal
quotes:
A store failure can leave a run's stored status behind its records. Any
request answered `internal_error` therefore stops the kernel once the
answer is sent, so the next start derives every run (rule 5) before any
request touches one.

| `internal_error` | the failing store change wrote nothing; changes the request made before it stay (Conventions); no detail (A16 rule 7) | the caller re-reads before repeating; the owner reads the host log |
precedent.why: The later rules define one attempt per request or startup recovery, an `internal_error` response and process stop on each store failure, with another recovery only on the next start.

topics.topic: Authoritative output and verdict when the recovery execution differs
questions: Because K-02 does not enforce that implementations depend only on inputs, which attempt's output is authoritative if the unrecorded execution and the recovery execution produce different values?
If an admitted function obtains time or chance by an undetected route and the rerun differs, which execution's output and verdict are authoritative?

judgement.why: This is the same question about which result is authoritative when replay differs, and the relevant texts have not changed since P15.

precedent.topic: Authoritative result and evidence when replay produces a different result
quotes:
Every concluded attempt at an element, every skipped node and every
`upstream_failed` node writes exactly one NodeExecution M23 — an owner's
resolution of an unknown outcome writes none (A11).

On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
`in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`: a
function element without a
concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect;
precedent.why: Only the recovered attempt that obtains a concluded NodeExecution becomes authoritative; the unrecorded attempt supplies no durable evidence.

topics.topic: Durable recovery marker and pinned rerun context when no trace exists
questions: If the execution leaves no trace record, what durable fact identifies that this particular run and node require recovery rather than having never started or already completed?

Which durable facts identify the unfinished execution and preserve the exact pinned implementation, input value or file, verdict context, and resource bounds needed for the rerun when the trace that names them does not exist?

quotes:
The run pins the flow version and, for every function node, the implementation
   of the current activation at start (M19). Nothing recorded later — a new
   activation, a new flow activation, a new binding — changes what the run
   executes.

Everything a resume or a restart needs is in the store before it is acted on:
   records of concluded attempts, decided approvals, and in-flight attempts before
   their request (K-17).

On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
   `in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
   run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
   from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
   waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
   outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
   kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`: a
   function element without a
   concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect;

The data directory holds one SQLite database with every kernel record, a
   content-addressed area of value bytes and file fixtures named by digest, and
   the run spool, one subdirectory per run.
judgement.why: The durable Run preserves the pinned implementation and inputs, persistent records and the run spool preserve restart context, and recovery identifies unfinished function elements by the absence of a concluded record in a still-running derived graph.

topics.topic: Handling trace refusal for operation nodes with possible external effects
questions: What prevents or handles the same trace-record refusal for an operation node, especially after its external effect may have happened?
What happens when the store refuses the trace record for an operation-node execution, especially when the operation may already have produced an external effect?

judgement.why: This is the same question about operation-node recovery after a refused outcome record and a possibly applied external effect, and the relevant texts have not changed since P1.

precedent.topic: Kernel handling of refused operation-node trace writes after possible external effects
quotes:
Everything a resume or a restart needs is in the store before it is acted on:
   records of concluded attempts, decided approvals, and in-flight attempts before
   their request (K-17).

On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
`in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`: a
function element without a
concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect; a `read`
element without one is sent again; an operation element of another class with
neither a concluded record nor an EffectAttempt was never sent and is advanced
as if reached for the first time — an approved, unused approval covers it
only while the rebuilt request has its `request_digest` (A10 rules 1 and 7).
precedent.why: State 2 identifies effect work with a pre-send EffectAttempt and identifies replayable function/read work from the durable run graph and absence of a concluded record.

topics.topic: Definition of store refusal and resolution of ambiguous trace commit acknowledgement
questions: Which persistence failures count as the store “refusing” the record, and how can recovery distinguish a definitely absent record from an acknowledgement lost after the record committed?

quotes:
`module:store`. Apply one named change of the closed set in one transaction, wholly or not at
all.
The records exist, all of them or none.

`internal_error` for any other broken invariant of its own, or a failed
transaction — nothing written either way.

On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
   `in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
   run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
   from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
   waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
   outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
   kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`: a
   function element without a
   concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect;
judgement.why: The later store contract makes a failed transaction definitely all-or-nothing, classifies it as internal_error, and startup reruns a function only when no concluded record is present, so a committed record prevents replay even if the prior caller did not observe success.
